claims.text: A critical combined Al and Cr concentration of at least 20 at.% promotes preferential formation of a protective oxide layer in NiCoCrFeAl-based HEAs.
The resulting protective layer is dense, continuous, and adherent.
The protective layer primarily consists of alpha-Al2O3 and/or Cr2O3.
Intrinsic sluggish diffusion and lattice distortion in HEAs impede oxygen ingress and excessive oxide-scale growth.
NiCoCrFeAl-based HEAs with lower Al and Cr concentrations form thicker oxide scales than high-Al/Cr variants.
NiCoCrFeAl-based HEAs with lower Al and Cr concentrations form less uniform and less protective oxide scales than high-Al/Cr variants.
The controlled comparison uses high- and low-Al/Cr compositional series while holding other compositional factors constant.
Initial characterization is intended to establish sample homogeneity and microstructure.
Both alloy series will be oxidized at 1000°C for 100 hours under identical controlled air/oxygen conditions.
SEM, TEM, and XRD characterization before oxidation is intended to reduce microstructural confounding.
At or above the proposed Al-plus-Cr threshold, Al and Cr preferentially oxidize to form stable oxide phases.
Sluggish diffusion in multi-principal-element systems limits oxygen penetration.
Limited oxygen penetration controls scale thickening and keeps the oxide thin, uniform, and protective.
Below the proposed Al-plus-Cr threshold, the protective oxide fails to form optimally.
The high-Al/Cr series will develop a thinner oxide layer than the low-Al/Cr baseline.
The high-Al/Cr series will develop a more uniform and adherent oxide layer than the low-Al/Cr baseline.
The high-Al/Cr series will exhibit lower oxide-growth kinetics than the low-Al/Cr baseline.
Microstructural heterogeneity and secondary phases could alter oxide formation.
The critical Al-plus-Cr threshold may vary with composition or processing.

contradictions.description: The exposure is repeatedly described as isothermal, but the intervention and conditions also specify identical or fixed thermal cycling. A genuinely isothermal hold and thermal cycling are distinct exposure protocols unless the cycling refers only to heat-up and cool-down.

The hypothesis and mechanism define the threshold as at least 20 at.% Al and Cr combined, whereas the material description says at least 20 at.% Al and Cr, which could be read as at least 20 at.% of each element.
